title: Learning Warm Starts for the Simplex Method from Measured Solver Cost
abstract: arXiv:2610.20892v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Learned warm starts for the simplex method build starting bases using predictions of which variables will be basic at optimality. Prior work has shown that starting bases predicted by graph neural networks can sharply reduce iteration counts, but the time saved may fall well short of the iterations saved. On 25 classes of linear programs (LPs), we find that a strong supervised basis predictor removes two thirds of the dual simplex's iterations but only a third of its time. Two effects explain the gap: the iterations removed by a good start tend to be cheap, and closeness to an optimal basis does not rank starts by cost. We prove that two starts with equal overlap with an optimal basis and equal pivot counts can differ in linear-algebra work by a factor that grows with the square root of the number of rows. Empirically, across the starts of one LP, the pivot count explains 71% of the variance of log solve time, while the CPU instruction

tldr: 该论文发现学习型热启动虽能消除单纯形法三分之二的迭代却只能节省三分之一的时间，其原因是被消除的迭代往往代价低廉且与最优基的接近程度无法反映实际计算成本，因此应以实测求解成本（如枢轴次数，可解释71%的对数求解时间方差）作为学习热启动的指导目标。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals why learned warm starts for the simplex method eliminate two-thirds of iterations but only one-third of solve time—removed iterations tend to be cheap and basis overlap does not rank starts by cost—and shows that measured solver cost, such as pivot count explaining 71% of log solve-time variance, should guide learning warm starts.
